subject: Usage-floor vs CapEx credit — exchange model for compliance add-ons
messages:
From: Jen Ortega <jen.ortega@pulsehealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing question — audit logs + KMS/HSM + residency (exchange idea)

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the call earlier. PulseHealth is evaluating Redwood for a multi-region deployment and we need firm pricing for audit logs (ingest + retention), a managed KMS path (and optional HSM seats), and data residency in our US-only VPC.

Our finance team prefers capitalized spend instead of ongoing surcharge where possible. They asked whether Redwood would consider an "exchange model": we commit to a one-time CapEx implementation or integration fee (paid up-front) in return for a lower usage floor or credits against the audit log surcharge over the first 12 months.

Two quick asks: can you (1) outline how you’d map a CapEx credit to the auditlog/KMS/HSM items (example math), and (2) flag any compliance/security constraints (SLA, evidence delivery cadence) that would change under that model?

I’ve attached a short spec of our auditlog retention needs (PH_AuditLog_Specs.pdf). Procurement copied.

Best,
Jen Ortega
Head of Finance (Interim)
PulseHealth

---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Jen Ortega <jen.ortega@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing question — audit logs + KMS/HSM + residency (exchange idea)

Jen — thanks for the note and the spec. Really appreciate the clarity.

Short answer: yes, we can structure an exchange model, but we need to align on a few levers so it’s predictable for both sides. I’m attaching a workbook with one illustrative construct (redwood-addon-pricing-exchange-model.xlsx) that shows examples for:
• CapEx amount exchanged for monthly credits against audit-log surcharge
• HSM seat amortization vs throughput-based concession
• Residency activation fee offset schedule

Notes up-front:
• Credits are amortized over a fixed period (typ. 12 months) and appear as a recurring invoice credit tied to the addon SKU; they do not reduce per-token usage pricing.
• HSM seats are typically handled as a monthly seat license; we can convert a portion of the CapEx into N months of seats (or a one-time onboarding credit).
• Evidence delivery (SOC/Security packet, penetration test attestations) is unchanged — those operational SLAs are independent of crediting and will follow the committed schedule in the SOW.

Aditya / Monica — can you confirm the viability of the following conservative matrix for PulseHealth and flag any legal/procurement constraints we should surface? Quick sketch: CapEx $250k -> $150k in auditlog credits over 12 months + 6 months HSM seat coverage for up to 3 seats + residency activation waived.

If that looks reasonable I’ll propose the sketch to Jen and set a 30-min workshop with procurement and our legal ops.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-addon-pricing-exchange-model.xlsx

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing question — Pricing construct for CapEx exchange model (internal)

Nikhil — copied Jen’s ask and your sketch. High level thoughts (internal):

1) Mapping logic:
   - Auditlog credits: map $ to GB-months retained based on PulseHealth profile (their spec shows ~4 TB/month ingest, 90-day hot retention). Use conservative ingest estimate to avoid under-crediting.
   - HSM: prefer to convert to seat months if they need deterministic keys for FIPS workflows — cheaper to cover seats up-front for pilot.
   - Residency: activation fee waiver is straightforward but must remain separate line item in SOW (for audit).

2) Accounting / invoicing:
   - CapEx payment recognized as Professional Services revenue; credits issued as contra-revenue on monthly invoices (legal wants explicit schedule).
   - Need to confirm revenue recognition with finance (Monica). If they want deferred revenue amortization, the legal SOW should mirror the credit schedule.

3) Risk & guardrails:
   - Non-refundable CapEx unless scope materially changes.
   - Credits expire if contract terminates early; pro-rata reclaim or offset on final invoice.
   - Limit credits to initial 12 months; beyond that, switch to standard addons pricing.

4) Example numbers (conservative):
   - CapEx: $250,000 upfront
   - Auditlog credit: $150,000 distributed $12,500/mo over 12 months -> covers audit ingest surcharge for ~X GB/month per our workbook.
   - HSM seats: 6 seat-months valued at $6,000 (covers 3 seats x 2 months) — or convert differently if client prefers longer seat duration.

Monica — please confirm whether finance is ok with (A) issuing monthly contra invoices as credits (we show them in HubSpot/AR) and (B) deferring professional services revenue over 12 months. Also legal: we should add a short clause that spells out credit expiration and remediation steps on early termination.

If both say go, Nikhil you can offer the sketched matrix and run a 30-min workshop. Happy to join for the procurement call.

—Aditya
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Jen Ortega <jen.ortega@pulsehealth.com>

• Legal will need the explicit credit schedule language and the early-termination reclaim example.

Procurement: can we schedule a 30-min workshop tomorrow at 11am PT to walk the matrix with Redwood (Nikhil + Aditya)? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and attach our PO template for alignment.

Jen Ortega
Head of Finance (Interim)
PulseHealth
